state:
MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT -- Schedule C: Service Level Penalties
Vendor: NimbusHost Cloud Services
Customer: Aldermere Financial Group
Effective Date: January 1, 2024

1. Definitions and Scope
This Schedule C governs service credits owed to Customer in the event Vendor's hosted platform
fails to meet the Monthly Uptime Guarantee defined below. Service credits are calculated against
Customer's Monthly Service Fee of $18,000.00 and are Customer's sole and exclusive remedy for
failure to meet the guarantee, except in cases of Vendor gross negligence or willful misconduct
as defined in Section 14 of the main Agreement.

2. Measurement Methodology
Uptime is measured as the percentage of five-minute intervals in a calendar month during which
the production environment successfully responded to Vendor's automated health-check probe from
at least two independent monitoring regions. Scheduled maintenance windows, communicated to
Customer at least 72 hours in advance and not exceeding 4 hours per calendar month, are excluded
from the uptime calculation entirely -- they count as neither uptime nor downtime. Any
maintenance window exceeding 4 hours in a given month, or any maintenance performed with less
than 72 hours' notice, is counted as downtime in full for purposes of this calculation.

3. Monthly Uptime Guarantee
Vendor guarantees 99.5% uptime in each calendar month, measured per Section 2 above.

4. Service Credit Tiers
If measured uptime in a calendar month falls below the 99.5% guarantee, Customer is entitled to
a service credit against that month's Monthly Service Fee according to the following tiers:
- Uptime of 99.0% up to (but not including) 99.5%: a credit of 5% of the Monthly Service Fee.
- Uptime of 98.0% up to (but not including) 99.0%: a credit of 10% of the Monthly Service Fee.
- Uptime below 98.0%: a credit of 25% of the Monthly Service Fee, which is the maximum credit
available under this Schedule regardless of how far below 98.0% the measured uptime falls.

For example, and for illustration only, this calendar month's measured uptime across the
production environment -- after excluding one properly-noticed 3-hour maintenance window on the
second Sunday of the month -- came in at 98.62%, based on the automated health-check logs
retained by Vendor's monitoring vendor. Under the tiers above, that figure falls within the
98.0%-to-99.0% band.

5. Claim Process
To receive a service credit, Customer must submit a written claim within 30 days of the end of
the affected calendar month, referencing the specific dates and times of any downtime Customer
independently observed. Vendor will reconcile Customer's claim against its own monitoring logs
described in Section 2 and issue any credit due within one billing cycle. Credits are applied to
the following month's invoice and are not paid out in cash. Failure to submit a claim within the
30-day window waives Customer's right to a credit for that month, even if Vendor's own logs
would otherwise support one.

6. Exclusions
Downtime caused by any of the following is excluded from the uptime calculation and does not
count against Vendor: (a) Customer's own misconfiguration of the environment; (b)
denial-of-service attacks not mitigated by Vendor's standard DDoS protection tier; (c) failures
of Customer's own upstream network provider; (d) force majeure events as defined in the main
Agreement.

7. Customer Success Summary (informational only, not part of the binding Schedule)
For internal tracking, the Customer Success team's monthly dashboard noted: "Uptime dipped this
month; estimate a $900 credit is due on next month's invoice pending Customer's claim." This
dashboard figure is a preliminary estimate only and is superseded by the actual tier calculation
in Section 4 above once a claim is processed.

8. Prior Terms
This Schedule C supersedes any prior service-level terms exchanged between the parties in
earlier statements of work, and applies uniformly across all environments (production, staging,
and disaster-recovery) covered by the Agreement unless a separate schedule expressly states
otherwise.
